title: Elemental Overload
wikitext:
{{Passive skill box|Elemental Overload}} '''Elemental Overload''' (often referred to as '''EO''') is a [[keystone]] [[passive skill]] that causes skills to deal 40% more [[elemental damage]] with [[hits]] and [[ailments]] for 8 seconds after that skill deals a [[critical strike]], but prevents any interactions between critical strikes and ailments. When the damage multiplier is active for a skill, it is indicated by a diamond on the bottom of that skill's icon in the skill bar. {{status | name = Elemental Overload | type = Keystone Effect |bonuses = ''Effect indicator seen below skill icon'' }} ==Mechanics== {{c|mod|Skills that have dealt a Critical Strike in the past 8 seconds deal 40% more Elemental Damage with Hits and Ailments}}: When a skill deals a [[critical strike]], it gains more elemental damage for 8 seconds, limited to [[hit]]s and [[ailments]]. * This damage bonus does not apply to the critical strike that caused Elemental Overload's effect to activate, only to hits while it is already active.https://www.pathofexile.com/forum/view-thread/3284453 * It does not apply to non-ailment [[damage over time]] such as {{il|Fire Trap}}'s [[burning ground]], even if it activates EO by critting. * This effect is not a [[buff]] or a skill effect; its duration cannot be affected by modifiers to [[duration|skill effect duration]] or expiration rate (e.g. {{il|Temporal Chains}}). Skills used by [[proxies]] such as [[totem]]s, [[trap]]s, or [[mine]]s will activate Elemental Overload for the player's skill when they crit, which will then apply to all uses of that skill, including by those proxies. [[Minions]] are unaffected by Elemental Overload, even the skill that summoned them can crit (e.g. {{il|Absolution}}). Per [[conversion]] mechanics, Elemental Overload's {{c|mod|40% more Elemental Damage}} will apply to physical damage converted into elemental, and elemental damage converted into chaos. Additionally, because inflicting damaging ailments with base damage of a different type is treated similar to [[conversion]], Elemental Overload will apply to [[poison]] originating from damage that was elemental at any point.https://www.reddit.com/r/pathofexile/comments/6aghcq/forum_announcements_damage_over_time_changes_more/dhg928v/?context=1 For example, [[poison]] inflicted with lightning damage damage through {{il|page=Volkuur's Guidance (Lightning)}}'s {{c|mod|Your Lightning Damage can Poison}}. {{c|mod|Ailments never count as being from Critical Strikes}}: This stat prevents your ailments from ever being counted as from a critical strike, even if the hit applying the ailment did critically strike. Consequentially, any {{c|mod|Damage over Time Multiplier for Ailments from Critical Strikes}} and similar conditional modifiers no longer apply. This includes the character's inherent +50% DoT multiplier on crit, passives like [[Dire Torment]], and gems like {{il|Critical Strike Affliction Support}}. * After an undocumented mechanical change in [[version 3.25.0]] (the stat text did not change), this stat also appears to prevent any conditional stats or interactions for ailments on critical strike.https://www.pathofexile.com/forum/view-thread/3560229/ For example, this prevents the inherent ability to apply elemental ailments on crit, and also prevents {{psl|Adder's Touch}} or {{psl|Secrets of Suffering}} from applying poison or alternate ailments on crit. Note that it does not prevent the application of ailments from chance-based sources or chill on a hit that critically strikes, though the ailment will not be considered from a crit and cannot be scaled through crit-related stats. :* If combined with {{psl|Perfect Agony}}, you will no longer be able to apply ailments with hits. ==Strategy== Elemental Overload is best allocated on characters that do not invest in [[critical strike]] but still deal critical strikes occasionally. Modifiers to critical strike multiplier no longer have any effect and can be ignored when assessing equipment. Ideally, when Elemental Overload is allocated, the player will strive to deal at least one critical strike every 8 seconds in order to keep the damage effect active. This can be achieved by balancing critical strike chance and hit rate. An average of one critical strike every 8 seconds is achieved by performing 12.5/(Critical Strike Chance) hits per second. For example, with the minimum critical strike chance of 5%, a character who performs 2.5 hits per second will on average deal a critical strike every 8 seconds (this assumes your accuracy for melee/ranged weapons allows a 100% chance to hit). ===Elemental Overload and Ignite=== Although the 40% More Elemental Damage modifier may seem less powerful than the +50% to damage over time multiplier an Ignite applied by a Critical Strike would apply, note that damage over time multipliers are additive with each other. EO's 40% More modifier, on the other hand, is multiplicative with all other modifiers. If you have at least +25% to your current DoT multiplier, EO will grant your Ignites more damage than the additional DoT multiplier with a crit. EO also only requires that you crit occasionally, rather than with each Ignite. ===Elemental Overload vs Critical Strikes?=== This table compares average damage of critical strikes versus elemental overload (with green indicating Elemental Overload is better than Critical Strikes). It assumes that you have a 100% uptime on elemental overload. The crit chance used in the table is effective crit chance, i.e. the real critical strike chance including accuracy.
